articles.body: MUMBAI: In a big boost to Mumbai, India's T20 captain Shreyas Iyer will join the team for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Super League matches in Nagpur, TOI has exclusively learnt. However, India's 2026 T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav, who led Mumbai in the league stage, will continue as the Mumbai captain for the Super League.In fact, with all-rounders Suryansh Shedge (it's understood that Shedge will be available from the second match) and Tanush Kotian also set to be available after India A's campaign in the Rising Stars Asia Cup in Doha ended on Thursday with their defeat against Sri Lanka A in the semi-finals, Mumbai will be at full strength for the Super League stage of the SMAT.Under Surya's captaincy, Mumbai remained unbeaten in the league phase, winning six out of their seven matches in Kolkata to collect 26 points, while the seventh game was washed out. With 214 runs in six matches at 53.50 and a strike rate of 230, including two fifties, SKY was Mumbai's second-highest run-getter and showed signs of returning to form.Iyer last featured in the white-ball series against New Zealand in October, comprising five T20Is followed by five ODIs, and did not enjoy great form. He scored 126 runs in five T20Is at 25.20, with a strike rate of 151.80, and just 86 runs in the ODIs at 16.75, without scoring a fifty. articles.title: Ball-tampering: Five memorable cricketing controversies
articles.summary: As Australia's use of sandpaper to alter the ball in 2018 dominates the cricket headlines, BBC Sport looks at other ball-tampering incidents.
articles.body:
It's the cricketing scandal which refuses to go away.

'Sandpapergate' first broke back in 2018 when Australia's Cameron Bancroft admitted he had tampered with the ball during a Test match against South Africa, with then-captain Steve Smith confessing that he knew of the plan in advance.

The fallout included bans for Smith, Bancroft and David Warner, but eight years later, the affair was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography . In it, he claimed the entire team knew about the ball-tampering, allegations denied by current Test captain Pat Cummins, one of the bowlers who played in that series.

Earlier this month, Cricket Australia set up an independent forum to explore the scandal and has now widened its scope to include the entire 2017-18 season, which includes the Ashes series against England.

Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report but it looks like a saga that is set to fill plenty more column inches before next summer's Ashes.

Tampering with the surface or seam of the ball helps cricketers find more aerodynamic swing when bowling it but it is strictly against the rules of the game - contravening Law 41, which deals with "unfair play".

"It's just not cricket" is a well-known British idiom indicating something is unfair or unsportsmanlike, which shows how deeply ingrained the sense of fair play is in the sport, and helps explain why ball-tampering is so frowned upon.

However, sandpapergate is by no means the first time that ball-tampering has barged its way to the top of cricket's news agenda. Here are some previous episodes that made the headlines.

Mike Atherton - England v South Africa, Lord's, 1994

England captain Mike Atherton was in the crosshairs in 1994 when he was accused of ball-tampering during the Lord's Test against South Africa.

After TV pictures appeared to show him applying dirt to the ball, Atherton insisted , external he had only "put some dust in my pocket from a used pitch... to keep my hands and the ball dry".

His defence was that, in trying to keep the moisture off the ball, he was therefore seeking to maintain its condition, rather than alter it.

There are varying accounts of exactly what Atherton told match referee Peter Burge, who chose a fine rather than a ban.

Sachin Tendulkar - South Africa v India, Port Elizabeth, 2001

Legendary India batsman Sachin Tendulkar was given a suspended one-match ban by match referee Mike Denness, after being found guilty of ball-tampering based on television footage during the second Test against South Africa.

Tendulkar was shown removing a piece of grass from the ball, and the International Cricket Council eventually decided this amounted to cleaning it without the umpire's permission rather than ball-tampering and so overturned the ban.

However, that was not the end of the controversy as the Indian cricket board refused to accept former England captain Denness as match referee for the third Test and it proceeded but was declared unofficial.

Punishment: Suspended one-match ban, overturned on appeal

Inzamam ul-Haq - England v Pakistan, The Oval, 2006

During the fourth day of the fourth Test between England and Pakistan, umpires Darrell Hair and Billy Doctrove held up play to call for a box of balls, and it soon became apparent that they had decided the tourists had illegally altered the condition of the ball.

The umpires awarded five penalty runs to England and offered them a replacement ball.

Bad light forced the players off shortly afterwards, and when the game resumed after tea Pakistan initially refused to take the field in protest, resulting in the first forfeited match in Test history.

Captain Inzamam-ul-Haq was held responsible for his team's actions but then cleared of the ball-tampering charge by an ICC tribunal. He was, however, banned for four matches for bringing the game into disrepute by refusing to resume play.

The result of the match was later changed to a draw, then altered again to an England win.

Punishment: Inzamam banned for four matches

Shahid Afridi - Australia v Pakistan, Perth, 2010

Pakistan captain Shahid Afridi was found guilty of ball-tampering during the fifth and final one-day international against Australia at the Waca in 2010, after he was caught by television cameras apparently biting the ball.

It was reported to the on-field umpires by the TV umpire and, after discussions with Afridi, the ball was changed. Pakistan lost the game, and series, 5-0.

Afridi's initial explanation was that he had been "trying to smell it and how it was feeling" but he admitted later he was "ashamed" of his actions, which had been "in the heat of the moment".

Punishment: Afridi banned for two T20 matches

Faf du Plessis - Australia v South Africa, Hobart 2016

The South Africa captain was caught on camera sucking on mints before using his saliva to shine the ball during the second Test against Australia.

Du Plessis was found guilty of ball-tampering by the International Cricket Council. He had previously been fined half his match fee for scuffing the ball on the zip of his trousers against Pakistan in 2013.

The charge did not result from any accusations by Australia but vice-captain David Warner told reporters afterwards: "We hold our heads high and I'd be very disappointed if one of our team members did that.

"The rules are in place for a reason. If you're not going to use them why bother having them?

"If you're going to overstep the mark, be prepared to get fined and miss Test matches."

Ironically, Warner's comments came back to bite him 16 months later.

Punishment: Du Plessis fined 100% of his match fee and given three penalty points

A version of this story was first published in 2018.

articles.title: 'He will win games single-handedly': Ex-cricketer backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World Cup
articles.summary: Former India captain and chief selector Kris Srikkanth has thrown his weight behind teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, backing him for
articles.body: Former India captain and chief selector Kris Srikkanth has thrown his weight behind teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, backing him for opportunities across formats and urging the Indian team management to consider him for the 2027 ODI World Cup.Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm with his extraordinary batting performances, showcasing remarkable power, timing and confidence at such a young age.Impressed by the youngster's fearless approach, Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi has the potential to become an all-format cricketer and should not be restricted to a particular format. Speaking on his YouTube channel, the former India opener also suggested that the teenager should be considered for the upcoming ODI series against Sri Lanka.Kris Srikkanth backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World CupSrikkanth believes Sooryavanshi deserves to be included in India's 15-member squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup, even if the team management is not yet convinced about his readiness for Test cricket. The former India selector stressed that the youngster should be given opportunities in the 50-over format to help him develop and gain experience at the international level."He is an all-format player. You don't want to play him in Tests, okay, but at least keep him in the 15. There is no questioning now. Sri Lanka will be coming for ODIs, give him a chance there. Put him in and let him play ODIs against them. If you really want to develop Suryavanshi, take him to the 2027 World Cup. Let him be in the 15. One day he will win you games single-handedly," Srikkanth said on his Youtube Channel.Srikkanth compares Sooryavanshi with Sachin Tendulkar and Virat KohliDrawing comparisons with two of India's greatest batting icons, Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, Srikkanth went a step further by describing Sooryavanshi as the "son of the god of cricket"."The way he is batting, power alone is not enough. You need timing as well. It is not just about power, it is also about his confidence. He looked so still and calm. He does not look ruffled. The greatest thing is that he knows exactly what he is doing. This is genius. First came the god of cricket, Sachin Tendulkar, then the King Virat Kohli, and now he is the son of the god of cricket," he said."If you do not encourage this guy and keep saying that he has to be groomed, it is unfair. You are going to spoil a cricketer this way. Team management and selectors, please wake up," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pakistan A beat Bangladesh A by five wickets to storm into Asia Cup Rising Stars final
articles.summary: Pakistan A defeated Bangladesh A by five wickets in the second semifinal of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 to secure a place in the final, where
articles.body: Pakistan A defeated Bangladesh A by five wickets in the second semifinal of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 to secure a place in the final, where they will face Sri Lanka A in Doha on Sunday. Chasing a target of 233, Pakistan A reached 233/5 in 45.2 overs, with Hasan Nawaz leading the way with a crucial 62-run knock. The victory also kept Pakistan A's unbeaten run in the tournament intact.Bangladesh A, meanwhile, were left to rue their inability to defend a competitive total despite a brilliant unbeaten century from Shahadat Hossain.Shahadat Hossain's unbeaten ton guides Bangladesh A to 232After winning the toss and electing to bat, Bangladesh A endured a disastrous start as Ali Raza struck twice inside the first five overs. Captain Saif Hassan and Mahmudul Hasan Joy also departed cheaply, leaving the side struggling at 15/4.Shahadat Hossain then took charge of the innings, building a crucial 95-run partnership with Mahidul Islam Ankon to revive Bangladesh A's hopes.Ankon contributed 42 runs, while SM Meherob added 28. Shahadat remained unbeaten on 103 off 118 deliveries, striking seven fours and three sixes, as Bangladesh A finished with 232/8 in their allotted 50 overs. For Pakistan A, Sufyan Moqim was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets for 29 runs. Hasan Nawaz and Ali Raza claimed two wickets each.Hasan Nawaz leads Pakistan A's successful chasePakistan A made a steady start to the chase but lost wickets at regular intervals, allowing Bangladesh A to remain in the contest.Hasan Nawaz, however, anchored the innings with a composed 62-run knock. His contribution proved crucial in keeping Pakistan A on course as they negotiated the target. Pakistan A eventually reached 233/5 in 45.2 overs to seal a five-wicket victory and advance to the final.Pakistan A to face Sri Lanka A in finalPakistan A will now take on Sri Lanka A in the title clash on Sunday, November 29, at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha. Sri Lanka A had booked their place in the final with an eight-wicket victory over India A in the first semifinal. They chased down India's 318-run target in just 41.3 overs, setting up a clash with Pakistan A for the tournament title.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sharjah Warriorz register first ILT20 Season 5 win with dominant victory over Dubai Capitals
articles.summary: Sharjah Warriorz registered their first win of ILT20 Season 5, cruising to a seven-wicket victory over Dubai Capitals at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on
articles.body: Sharjah Warriorz registered their first win of ILT20 Season 5, cruising to a seven-wicket victory over Dubai Capitals at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Friday.A disciplined bowling display, led by Junaid Siddique's impressive figures of 3/25, restricted the Capitals to 126 in 19.4 overs. Adam Milne and Richard Gleeson chipped in with two wickets apiece, returning figures of 2/19 and 2/23 respectively.The Warriorz made light work of the chase, reaching 130/3 in just 13 overs. Tim Seifert and Paul Walter provided the perfect platform with an explosive opening stand of 82 runs, scoring 41 off 20 balls and 42 off 25 balls respectively. Brandon McMullen remained unbeaten on 26 off 19 deliveries to complete the victory with 42 balls to spare.Karim Janat top-scored for the Capitals with 30 off 18 balls, but his contribution was not enough to prevent his side from suffering their second all-out dismissal in three matches.Dubai Capitals struggle after early setbacksThe Capitals endured a difficult start after being asked to bat, managing just three runs in the first two overs. Milne and Gleeson kept the opening batters under pressure before Siddique provided the first breakthrough.Masood Gurbaz, who had struggled to get going, struck Siddique for a six in the final over of the powerplay but could not capitalise on it. The pacer dismissed him shortly afterwards, with Gurbaz departing for 17 off 22 balls to leave Dubai at 32/1.Paul Walter then removed Max Holden for just one run off seven deliveries, before Sikandar Raza accounted for Faf du Plessis (15 off 19) in the following over. The Capitals were reduced to 40/3.Siddique returned to strike again with the opening delivery of the 12th over, sending back skipper Sam Billings, who was caught behind for 12 off nine balls. The dismissal came after Dubai had collected 16 runs from Raza's 11th over.Marcus Stoinis briefly counter-attacked, smashing two consecutive sixes in that over, but his innings of 23 off 13 balls ended when Sharafuddin Ashraf dismissed him in the 13th over. Siddique then removed Rovman Powell (2 off 8) in the 14th over, leaving the Capitals reeling at 78/6.Janat attempted to revive the innings, combining with Hassan Khan for a 44-run partnership off 27 deliveries. Janat contributed 30 off 18 balls, while Hassan scored 18 off 15. The pair also took 16 runs from the 16th over to give their side some momentum.However, the Warriorz bowlers finished strongly. Milne picked up two wickets in the 19th over, before Gleeson dismissed Janat and Dushmantha Chameera off successive deliveries in the final over to bowl the Capitals out for 126.Seifert, Walter make short work of the chaseIn reply, the Warriorz openers came out firing and put the Capitals attack under immediate pressure. Seifert and Walter took 18 runs off Chameera's only over, which included two sixes, before collecting 14 off Tymal Mills and 20 off Stoinis in consecutive overs.Their aggressive approach took Sharjah to 79/0 at the end of the powerplay, leaving them firmly in control of the chase.Muhammad Arfan eventually broke the opening partnership in the seventh over, with Seifert caught behind by Billings for 41 off 20 balls. Walter's entertaining knock ended in the ninth over when Noor Ahmad bowled him for 42 off 25 deliveries.The Afghanistan spinner struck again in the 11th over, having James Rew caught for 10 off nine balls as the Warriorz slipped to 111/3.However, the target was never out of reach. articles.title: Nathan Lyon dropped by Australia for their Test series against New Zealand
articles.summary: Nathan Lyon was left out of Australia's 13-player squad for their Test series against New Zealand, which starts on December 9 in Perth; Uncapped off-spinner Corey Rocchiccioli comes into the squad; Lyon was omitted from Australia's second Test vs South Africa
articles.body:
The 39-year-old off-spinner, who has been a mainstay for the Baggy Greens for 13 years, will be replaced by Western Australia's Corey Rocchiccioli.

Lyon has not spoken publicly since Usman Khawaja's explosive Sandpapergate claims were published in his autobiography.

Australia selection chair George Bailey confirmed that his omission was not related to the ongoing saga, and was based on performances.

"Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches," said Bailey.

"We also know he has an extraordinary record and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward."

Other notable omissions include Marnus Labuschagne, Cooper Connolly and Beau Webster, with middle-order batter Jack Clayton being drafted into the squad and is in line to make his debut during the series.

In recent years, Lyon has seen his role with the Test side diminished, with a right hamstring injury, sustained during day five of the third Ashes Test in 2025, ruling him out of Test selection for eight months.

Lyon, who ranks second as Australia's all-time leading wicket-taker behind Shane Warne with 577 wickets from 145 Tests, had previously been dropped for the second Ashes Test at The Gabba and spoke openly about the omission, saying he was "filthy" and "gutted" about being dropped .

Lyon had also been omitted from Australia's second Test against South Africa in October.

Prior to last year's Test at The Gabba, the off-spinner had remarkably not been left out of a Test squad since he made his debut in 2011.

Uncapped off-spinner Rocchiccioli will likely go head-to-head with Scott Boland for a spot in the side to play New Zealand on the fiery Perth pitch in the first Test which starts on December 9.

"Corey has been a strong performer in domestic cricket for the past few seasons and has traits that are well suited to Australian conditions," Bailey said.

Under-scrutiny skipper Pat Cummins will captain the side, while Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Steve Smith, who have all found themselves at the centre of Australia's recent Sandpapergate saga, were also named in the team.

Smith had missed Australia's final Test against South Africa in Cape Town with a neck injury.

Australia will add one final player after the sixth round of Sheffield Shield matches.

articles.title: 'Siraj needs help': R Ashwin urges India team to show compassion after pacer's repeated snubs
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin has urged the Indian team management and players to show compassion towards Mohammed Siraj following the fast bowler's consecutive
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin has urged the Indian team management and players to show compassion towards Mohammed Siraj following the fast bowler's consecutive omissions from the playing XI in the two-Test series against New Zealand. The former India spinner believes Siraj needs emotional support and someone in the dressing room who can offer a patient hearing without passing judgement.Drawing from his own experience, Ashwin stressed that such difficult phases can affect players differently and that having a sports psychologist around could make a significant difference. He also suggested that Siraj needs a father-like or mother-like figure within the team who can help him deal with the disappointment and provide clarity about his situation.Speaking on his YouTube show Ash ki Baat, Ashwin said being left out can naturally lead to frustration and negative thoughts, making it important for teammates to understand what a player is going through."I hope people give him a little compassion, because in such a situation you feel horrible and you go into a complaining zone, it's natural," Ashwin said.The veteran spinner explained that players respond differently when they are dropped, and team management often gets an opportunity to understand their personalities through such situations. According to him, those who react negatively are not necessarily difficult to handle but may simply need someone to listen to them.Ashwin emphasised that a psychologist could play an important role in such circumstances, particularly when a player finds it difficult to open up to people around him."If he (Siraj) starts saying negative things, first he needs somebody to listen to him," Ashwin said. "That's why teams need a psychologist. At this time, Siraj will want to say what's in his mind and heart, but he won't trust anyone enough to say it, because that is where he is. Someone should listen to him, soak up what's going on in his mind, understand his mindset, then whatever he has to work on, you can tell him, whether it's fitness, bowling speed, bowling rhythm, anything."Sports psychologists are an established part of several high-performance sporting set-ups across the world. With an understanding of both sport and psychological principles, they help athletes deal with challenges such as performance anxiety, insecurity and motivation-related issues.The Indian women's team has recently worked with a psychologist, but the men's team has not had one on a full-time basis for several years.Siraj's omission has attracted attention given his standing in India's bowling attack. He is the country's highest wicket-taker in the ongoing World Test Championship cycle, yet was left out of the first Test against New Zealand in favour of Prasidh Krishna. The right-arm pacer was overlooked again for the second Test, with debutant Gurnoor Brar getting the nod.India captain Shubman Gill has maintained that the decisions were based on form. However, there have also been murmurs that Siraj's style of bowling has not gone down particularly well with bowling coach Morne Morkel.Ashwin believes the immediate priority should be to ensure that Siraj has someone within the dressing room with whom he can speak freely, without worrying about being judged."In this situation, Siraj needs clarity and a father-type or mother-type figure in that team who is ready to listen to whatever is on his mind without judging," Ashwin said.The former India spinner also pointed out that Siraj had continued to conduct himself as a team player despite the disappointment of missing out. He recalled how the pacer went up to Gurnoor, spoke to him and congratulated him on his opportunity."If both things happen, we can hold on to Siraj. But I really feel, his face today, he's trying to be a teamman; he went and spoke to Gurnoor, praised him, he is doing whatever he can from his side. I really do feel sorry for him, and he needs help," Ashwin added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

He has been particularly prolific in the ongoing Sheffield Shield campaign, scoring 449 runs from nine innings at an average of 74.83, including a century and four fifties.Rocchiccioli, meanwhile, has claimed 18 wickets in the Sheffield Shield this season at an average of 33.88. The 29-year-old has an overall tally of 205 wickets from 59 first-class appearances, with six five-wicket hauls to his name.There are several other changes to Australia's squad that featured in the third Test against South Africa. Marnus Labuschagne, Beau Webster, Cooper Connolly and Matthew Kuhnemann have all been left out, while Nic Maddinson and Sam Harper, who were released ahead of that Test, have not been recalled.Labuschagne endured a disappointing outing in South Africa, finishing the series with 131 runs from six innings at an average of 21.83. articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd Test: Akash Deep triggers New Zealand collapse, but Tom Blundell leads fightback against India
articles.summary: Two absences made their presence felt at Hagley Oval on Friday: Pacer Mohammed Siraj from India’s playing XI, again, and, more alarmingly, the usual
articles.body: Two absences made their presence felt at Hagley Oval on Friday: Pacer Mohammed Siraj from India’s playing XI, again, and, more alarmingly, the usual magic, speed and spark in spearhead Jasprit Bumrah’s bowling. It meant that despite Akash Deep’s brilliant spell in the post-lunch session (7-4-7-2), which triggered a New Zealand mini-collapse from 110-1 to 110-4, the hosts still managed to claim bragging rights as they ended Day One of the second Test on 246/5.Wicketkeeper-batter Tom Blundell was instrumental in that recovery, scoring an unbeaten 53 and featuring in two key partnerships — a 74-run stand with Daryl Mitchell (31) for the fifth wicket and an unbroken 62-run association with Glenn Phillips (36*).Despite India keeping the Kiwi batters on a tight leash for large portions of the day, they will still wonder if the advantage of winning the toss and bowling first on a greenish pitch has been squandered. Akash was comfortably India’s most impressive bowler. He produced two superb deliveries to remove the wellset Tom Latham (59) and Rachin Ravindra (0), finishing with 2/52 from 21 overs.The Indian team management will wonder if their bowlers made the batters play enough in the first session, as too many deliveries were left alone. Latham survived an LBW decision against Bumrah in the opening over after DRS showed the ball had pitched marginally outside leg stump, overturning Richard Illingworth’s ‘out’ call. Akash, too, could have removed Latham on 29, but KL Rahul spilled an edge at second slip.It needed debutant Gurnoor Brar to strike with the final ball before lunch, trapping Conway LBW to end a gritty 77-run opening partnership.India then bossed the second session. Akash, benefiting from a change of ends, unleashed a beauty from around the stumps that came in with the angle, pitched and left the batter and took Latham’s outside edge. Kamboj, who was too short in his opening spell, had Henry Nicholls top-edge a pull to Akash at long leg.Akash struck again, inducing Ravindra into a tentative prod outside off stump. India seemed to be taking control but Blundell and Mitchell dug in and started tiring the Indian bowlers out. Once the ball softened, batting became easier.As they had been in Wellington, India were profligate in Christchurch too. Anshul Kamboj missed a run-out chance to dismiss Nicholls. Substitute Nitish Reddy also missed a run-out chance to send back Blundell. In between, Rishabh Pant put down two difficult chances.Picked ahead of Ravindra Jadeja, Washington Sundar was introduced in the 61st over and he had Mitchell caught smartly by Dhruv Jurel at leg slip. But Blundell, playing his 50th Test, reached his halfcentury before joining Phillips in frustrating India. Even the second new ball failed to trouble them.India, though, will now be worried about Bumrah. The leader of the attack went wicketless in 19 overs, conceding just 37 runs, but the numbers told only part of the story. Despite being well rested, he bowled largely in the high 120s and low 130s and appeared short of his customary gallop and menace. He created half-chances, experimented with a different action and looked unfit.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: MUMBAI: Will it prove to be a masterstroke or a step backward?
articles.body: MUMBAI: Will it prove to be a masterstroke or a step backward? Mumbai Indians have turned to the man who led them to five IPL titles between 2013 and 2020, reinstating Rohit Sharma as captain for IPL 2027.Hoping to rediscover their best form and end their wait for a sixth title, MI are banking on the 39-year-old former India captain for one final stint at the helm. TOI had reported his return on Oct 31 (see box).Rohit’s return was cleared once Hardik Pandya, MI captain for the past three seasons, moved to Punjab Kings in a highprofile trade involving pacer Arshdeep Singh. MI had hinted at the change with a cryptic social media post a couple of days ago. Tilak Varma, a long-term captaincy prospect, is likely to be named vice-captain.The captaincy change follows a major overhaul of MI’s coaching staff, with Kieron Pollard replacing Mahela Jayawardene as head coach. Former India batter Robin Uthappa has been appointed batting coach while former India fielding coach T Dilip will take charge of the fielding department.“I’m ready for the 20th season of the IPL. The focus will be on playing our brand of cricket, competing together and enjoying the game. Mumbai Indians has been a huge part of my life, and leading this team has always been something,” Rohit said in a release issued by the franchise.Rohit first became MI captain midway through the 2013 season, taking over from Ricky Ponting and leading the team to its maiden IPL title at Eden Gardens in Kolkata.Rohit led MI to five IPL titles (2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020) and the 2013 Champions League T20 crown. After MI’s last title in 2020, their results dipped, with the team finishing fifth in 2021, last in 2022, and exiting in Qualifier 2 in 2023.Rohit’s poor run with the bat and the team’s lack of success led to his removal as captain ahead of IPL 2024, with Hardik Pandya taking over.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ: Has the 'Boom' gone missing? Jasprit Bumrah's dip in pace raises concerns for India
articles.summary: Since his first back injury in 2018, India have treated Jasprit Bumrah like a precious jewel.
articles.body: Since his first back injury in 2018, India have treated Jasprit Bumrah like a precious jewel. His workload has been meticulously managed, formats have been prioritised and bilateral series sacrificed to ensure their smoking gun is ready to fire when India need him most: in marquee Test series and ICC events.Which is precisely why what unfolded at the Hagley Oval on Friday should be a worry. Bumrah finished Day One of the second Test against New Zealand wicketless after 19 overs. The figures, 0/37, were economical. But are the numbers concealing more than they are revealing?One of Bumrah’s great gifts has been to rush batters with the zip he gets off the pitch because of his wrist snap and the fact that batters do not get a trigger movement when facing him — his delivery point is ahead of others. What was troubling on Friday was the absence of that zip. As the day wore on, his pace frequently hovered around 127-130 kmph. More strikingly, he appeared to be searching for rhythm, experimenting with different runups and tweaks to his action.India great Sunil Gavaskar too noticed something amiss. “With the second new ball, Bumrah hasn’t looked even dangerous, like he did with the first new ball. In Wellington, on the first day, he looked really threatening, and even in the second innings, he looked threatening,” Gavaskar said on Sony Sports Network.The former India captain was particularly concerned by the difference in intensity when Bumrah returned with the second new ball. “When the second new ball came, it didn’t seem that he had that zip or anything. He has bowled 15 or 16 overs (19); maybe he was feeling the effects,” Gavaskar said.“That is where India is struggling. If you are not going to get wickets with the second new ball, then you would have to spend longer hours in the field.”And that is where India’s concern lies. This is not someone who has reached New Zealand after being flogged across formats. He did not play against Sri Lanka or the West Indies and sat out the white-ball leg in New Zealand. He has not played an ODI since the England series in July.The idea behind such management is obvious: reduce the mileage on a rare talent and an injury-prone body, and have Bumrah fresh for key assignments. New Zealand was one of them, considering crucial WTC points were at stake.Yet, after taking five wickets in Wellington, Bumrah’s potency diminished. At Hagley, his wicket drought stretched to 220 balls, the third-longest of his Test career.The experimenting with his run-up added another layer of intrigue. Former New Zealand spinner Ish Sodhi noticed Bumrah changing his set-up even between deliveries, while Akash Deep felt too much is being made of it.“He’s Bumrah. If he’s doing something, then there must be some thought behind it. What can we comment on that? He was even doing it in the practice sessions, so there must be some plan in his mind,” Akash, who benefited from Bumrah’s constant advice from mid-off, said.Perhaps there is. Fast bowlers constantly tinker with rhythm and mechanics. But can India ignore the larger question? If they fail to qualify for the WTC final, which seems highly likely, what should Bumrah’s Test workload look like after the BorderGavaskar Trophy?At this stage of his career, India may need to become even more ruthless about distinguishing between Tests where Bumrah is indispensable and those where preserving him for bigger assignments makes more sense.India have spent years ensuring Bumrah bowls fewer overs so that the overs he does bowl remain special. But what should the team do when those overs start looking laboured despite that preservation?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: No ‘pole hunting’: Akash Deep reaps rewards of discipline
articles.summary: India’s bowling coach and former South Africa pacer Morne Morkel had urged India’s bowlers on the eve of the second Test not to go “pole hunting” and not
articles.body: India’s bowling coach and former South Africa pacer Morne Morkel had urged India’s bowlers on the eve of the second Test not to go “pole hunting” and not to get “desperate for wickets”. He had stressed that on a surface with plenty of grass and the potential to offer carry, staying patient and consistently hitting the right areas would do the job.On Friday, Akash Deep showed he had been all ears. India went largely unrewarded in the pre-lunch session, despite the bowlers getting considerable movement and producing 26 false shots. However, Akash responded after lunch with a disciplined spell that helped trigger New Zealand’s slide to 110 for four.His mantra was simple: make the batter play. “In the first session, there was some moisture in the pitch, and because of that, the ball wasn’t coming on to the bat with much pace, so the edges weren’t carrying,” Akash explained. “Early on, we were also moving the ball a bit too much. After lunch, we decided to focus on bowling in good areas and being patient. That was our plan, and it helped us pick up three wickets.”It was almost a perfect illustration of Morkel’s point. Rather than searching for the magic delivery, India concentrated on creating opportunities. Akash produced two himself. Bowling round the wicket, he angled one into Tom Latham before getting it to straighten and take the outside edge of the New Zealand captain, who had battled his way to 59.He then dismissed Rachin Ravindra for a duck, again forcing the left-hander to play at a good-length delivery outside off. “My focus was on making the batter play as many deliveries as possible,” Akash said. “I bowled five or six overs in my first spell and tried to get the batter playing at 80-90 per cent of the deliveries.”That figure summed up his approach. On a surface where extravagant movement could tempt a seamer into searching for wickets, Akash concentrated on bringing the batter into play.India could not, however, sustain their post-lunch dominance. From 110 for four, New Zealand recovered to 246 for five through Tom Blundell’s unbeaten 53. He added 74 with Daryl Mitchell (31) before forging an unbroken 62-run partnership with Glenn Phillips (36 not out).“As the ball gets older, batting becomes a little easier,” Akash said. “We have to keep the runs down as well because we don’t want to let the opposition get away. We can’t always attack; we have to balance that with controlling the scoring.”Blundell’s assessment underlined why discipline was vital. “Throughout the whole day, it was moving a lot,” he said. “It was a wicket where you never feel in as a batter.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
